canonical_name: TinyEKF -- a header-only Extended Kalman Filter in C for microcontrollers and PCs (Simon D. Levy)
lineage: The Extended Kalman Filter (Schmidt/Smith, NASA Apollo era, 1960s) reduced to a few hundred lines with static allocation for Arduino/Teensy-class hardware; shipped with a GPS position/velocity example whose data and reference implementation come from Rachel Blakeley's 'Extended Kalman Filter for GPS' (MATLAB). SMALL MECHANISM: predict, then update with a linearised measurement model.
version: github.com/simondlevy/TinyEKF master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)
entry_points: src/tinyekf.h: ekf_initialize / ekf_predict / ekf_update; the GPS example

example.command: build and run the shipped GPS example on its gps.csv
example.output: the receiver position/clock trajectory; compared against the example's reference output

upstream_docs: Blakeley, Extended Kalman Filter for GPS (the example's source)

human_capability_summary.built_to: estimate a hidden state (position, clock bias) from nonlinear noisy measurements on a machine with kilobytes of RAM
human_capability_summary.pressure: hidden state, measurement noise, nonlinearity (ranges), tiny memory and CPU budgets
human_capability_summary.success_means: the estimate converges to the true trajectory and the covariance shrinks; no dynamic allocation

human_environmental_pressure: noisy observation, hidden state, bounded memory
human_failure_condition: filter divergence: linearisation error or a bad noise model drives the covariance to inconsistency and the estimate away
behavioral_entry_point: scale the measurement-noise matrix R or corrupt a satellite's range and watch the estimate/covariance respond

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run tinyekf-levy
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: estimate a hidden state (position, clock bias) from nonlinear noisy measurements on a machine with kilobytes of RAM
